pairs.subject: agent-host-experience
pairs.evidence: app/_server/mcp/rpc.ts:112 tools/list publishes the same catalog to every token whatever its scope, so a read-scope agent's model sees the launch and job writes it can only be refused on; the standard asks for a catalog computed from what the role is granted, and the money-bearing path's pending spend request has no expiry or reaper.

techniques.evidence: app/_server/mcp/rpc.ts:112 Five family tools with paged, filtered reads, blast-radius descriptions and in-band {code, detail, reason} refusals do follow the technique. Two gaps: the catalog depends only on the projection mode, not on the agent's grant (scope is checked per call, rpc.ts callTool), and no read has a concise/detailed response mode.

packages/domain/src/mcp.ts:39 Money comes home correctly: a non-free live launch is filed as a spend request and the operator confirms it on the Board (launch.ts:44), with an opaque sr_ id and a /board link. But a pending request never expires and nothing reaps it (creation-names-reaper). The answer has no sentence saying nothing has happened yet; that is said only once, in the initialize instructions.

app/_server/mcp/rpc.ts:106 Only the tools capability is declared; there are no resources and no ui:// view resources, so no rendered view ships. The text floor holds: every result carries text plus structuredContent.
app/_server/mcp/rpc.ts:55 Results are text plus structured JSON. No declarative view spec is projected outward; `view` is only a deep-link path.
app/_server/mcp/rpc.ts:17 This door is the outside tier (the tool protocol). It does not drive the product's own windows, so it keeps the two tiers apart as the standard asks.
app/api/mcp/route.ts:1 Capability form only: a stateless tool server with no agent card and no task lifecycle. That is the default the standard recommends.
